visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 correctly depicts the internally tangent nested circles with the appropriate alternating shaded rings and highlights the correct ring/total structure, while Lesson 2 largely lacks a circle diagram and its Desmos graph is visually mis-scaled so the target line/intersection are not actually shown in the plotted view.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 1 includes a well-formed, wired quiz gate with a real question, plausible options, a correct answer, and remediation path after a specific act, whereas Lesson 2 has no available gate specs or plan and therefore no functioning checkpoints.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 1 has clearer, well-paced, naturally segmented narration with spoken math rendered mostly intelligibly, while Lesson 2 is a long unsegmented monologue with an awkward repetitive ending and less polished phrasing.

sync.rationale: Lesson 1 provides timed visual cues that are mostly aligned with the narrated references, while Lesson 2 has no beat or cue timing data at all, making visual-narration synchronization impossible to verify and therefore much weaker on this dimension.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 correctly derives the single-ring area and total-area formula step by step before solving the inequality, while Lesson 2 gives the correct formula and answer but largely treats the key area formula as a Desmos input without explaining why it represents the shaded area.

polish.rationale: Lesson 1 has a cleaner, more consistent centered split-screen layout with readable math and minimal clutter, while Lesson 2 is dominated by extraneous app/player/chat UI, large empty spaces, truncated text, cursors, and caption overlays that make the presentation much less polished.

aggregator.explanation: All six dimension agents strongly prefer Lesson 1, with high confidence across visual accuracy, interactivity, narration quality, synchronization, concept accuracy, and polish. Lesson 1 is credited with an accurate and clear circle diagram, functioning quiz interaction, better-paced narration, aligned timed visual cues, a step-by-step derivation of the area formula and inequality, and a cleaner presentation. Lesson 2 is consistently weaker due to missing or mis-scaled visuals, lack of interactive checkpoints, unsegmented narration, no synchronization data, less explanation of the core formula, and cluttered UI/polish issues.
